checklist.edge_construction_module: Implemented implicitly via PyG TemporalData; src/dst pairs and per-flow msg act as edges

statistical_disentanglement.paper: Eq. 5–7: SMT-style optimization of per-feature weight vector w to maximize differentiation between adjacent features under a simplex constraint.
statistical_disentanglement.ours: Smooth differentiable surrogate of Eq. 5: maximize mean(|2 w_i F_i − w_{i−1} F_{i−1} − w_{i+1} F_{i+1}|) plus boundary term, with a soft simplex penalty (w∈(0,1) via sigmoid). Trained jointly with the rest of the model.
statistical_disentanglement.deviation: We avoid an external SMT solver; instead we optimize a smooth surrogate of the same objective. This is documented in the report.

representational_disentanglement.paper: Eq. for orthogonality of element-wise edge representation components.
representational_disentanglement.ours: RD module that produces K=4 group projections (group_dim=16), with batch-mean group vectors regularized to be near-orthogonal (||V V^T − I||² penalty).

dynamic_memory.paper: Eq. 10: GRU-based memory update; sinusoidal time encoder.

multi_layer_graph_diffusion.paper: Multi-layer (l_i=0/1) PM-style continuous diffusion with layer-temporal coefficient s_ij.
multi_layer_graph_diffusion.ours: Approximated with multi-scale message-passing depths (1/2/3 hops) on the running TGN memory; the dataset has src_layer=dst_layer=0 for every flow, so we cannot exercise the multi-layer branch but we still implement the multi-scale fusion that the paper uses for few-shot.
multi_layer_graph_diffusion.deviation: All flows in the provided NF-UNSW-NB15-v2 file lie in layer 0, so the explicit l_i/l_j layer term reduces to a constant. The non-trivial part of the diffusion (multi-scale fusion of node states) is preserved.

multi_scale_representation_fusion.ours: Concatenation of three diffusion depths (scale 1, 2, 3) before classification head.

loss.paper: L = L_int + α L_smooth + β L_dis
loss.ours: L = CE_binary + 0.5 CE_multiclass + α L_SD + β L_RD; α=β=0.05. We omit L_smooth (temporal smoothness over X_t) because we use a memory snapshot rather than per-timestamp embeddings.
